title: The hub run: pack, carry, hand over, bring back
purpose: Every phone that recorded today reaches the hub tonight and comes back empty before the shift, with a name signed against it at every step, so one crash, one theft, or one checkpoint costs a third of a site and never the site.
with: the Portfolio Manager at the site, the hub attendant at the hub, and the anchor who opens the device room in the morning
when: Every night at a hub site, after the Portfolio Manager's end-of-day review, with the last run at the hub before 11 PM. Then again early in the morning, so the phones are back before the 7:00 AM clock-in. On Thursday every factory phone goes; the hub clears and charges them on Friday, the day off, and they come back before Saturday's shift. Hotels keep running on their own lines.
takes: The evening, in at least three round trips to the hub, and the early morning to bring the phones back. Above 60 phones, two runners on staggered runs.
needs: Tonight's run from the Portfolio Manager: the site, the hub, and how many runs
The vehicle, fueled before the first run, because you never stop en route
One locked, unmarked hard case per run, and its key
A printed manifest for each case: device IDs, count, site, time out, runner name
The letter kit: the Arabic company letter on letterhead, signed and stamped, a copy of the commercial register, the device list, and two phone numbers that answer
Your own phone, charged, with Moharam's number in it

steps.do: Get tonight's run from the Portfolio Manager before you drive to the site: the site, the hub, and how many runs.
steps.detail: The site plan names the closest hub: the central hub downtown, Sheikh Zayed, or the Fifth Settlement. Take the hub from the site plan every night, never from memory. A run carries a third of the site's phones at most, so a site of 30 phones is three runs of ten. Above 60 phones a second runner works staggered runs, and Moharam says who takes which.
steps.check: You can say the site, the hub, and how many phones go in each run before you start the engine.

steps.do: Check the letter kit in your bag and call one of the two numbers on it.
steps.detail: The Arabic company letter on letterhead with your name, the device count, today's date, the signature, and the company stamp. A copy of the commercial register. The device list. Two phone numbers that answer. This is what a checkpoint asks for, so it rides in your bag on every run, never inside the case. If anything is missing, call Moharam before you drive. You do not run without the letter.
steps.check: Every piece is in your bag and the number you called answered.

steps.do: At the site, count this run's phones into the case against the manifest, with the Portfolio Manager.
steps.time: After the Portfolio Manager's end-of-day review
steps.detail: The Portfolio Manager holds the device room until you have counted and signed, and hands you the manifest for this case: device IDs, count, site, time out, your name. Count by device number, one phone at a time, as each goes into the case. Never more than a third of the site's phones in one case, one vehicle, or one run. Every phone marked full goes on the first run, so the hub flushes it first.
steps.check: The phones in the case are the phones on the manifest, and the count is a third of the site's phones or less.

steps.do: Put the manifest inside, lock the case, and keep the key on you.
steps.detail: The case is a locked, unmarked hard case. Nothing on the outside says phones or names the company. One manifest per case, inside with the phones. The key stays in your pocket, never in the case and never left at the site or the hub.
steps.check: The case is locked, the outside says nothing, and the manifest is inside.

steps.do: Have the Portfolio Manager confirm on the MDM map that every phone in the case shows.
steps.detail: Location tracking is on for every phone in transit. A phone on the manifest that is not on the map does not travel until it is. A phone the map cannot see is a phone nobody can find on the road.
steps.check: Every device ID on the manifest is on the MDM map before the case leaves the room.

steps.do: Sign custody at pickup, you and the Portfolio Manager, before the case leaves the room.
steps.detail: Two signatures, the count, the time out, and the hub you are driving to, on the manifest. No signature, no handover. From this signature until the drop signature, these phones are yours.
steps.check: Both signatures are on the pickup line with the count and the time out.

steps.do: Drive straight to the hub. Never stop en route.
steps.detail: Site to hub and nothing in between: no fuel, no food, no passenger, no errand. Keep your own phone on and answer it. If Moharam sends you to the second hub, you go there and nowhere else. Nobody takes a case home, not for an hour. Phones live at the site, at a hub, or in a signed-for case, nowhere else.
steps.check: You arrive at the hub with the case locked, and you did not stop between the site and the hub.

steps.do: At a checkpoint, pull over, stay calm, hand over the letter, the commercial register copy, and the manifest, and call Moharam.
steps.detail: Open the case so the officer sees the phones and the manifest that lists them. Say what it is in plain words: company phones, going between a company site and the company's upload facility, and give the exact count on the manifest. Point to the two numbers on the letter; Moharam takes the officer's call. If anyone asks what the work is, it is video for a robotics research program, nothing more. Never argue, never hide the count, never name the client. Call Moharam from the checkpoint: where you are, who is asking, what they want. If the phones or the papers are held, get a written receipt with the count, who holds them, and where, before you drive on. Mano brings counsel the same day.
steps.check: The officer has seen the letter, the register copy, and the manifest, Moharam has heard from you from the checkpoint, and anything held has a receipt in your hand.

steps.do: At the hub, open the case and let the attendant count against the manifest, then both of you sign custody at drop.
steps.detail: The attendant reads every device ID and ticks it, counts the phones, and writes the case into the hub log. When the count matches, you both sign with the time in. No signature, no handover, and you do not leave before both signatures are on the page. From that signature the phones are the hub's.
steps.check: The attendant's count is the manifest count, and both signatures are on the drop line with the time in.

steps.do: Go back for the next run, and keep going until every phone that recorded today is at the hub, with the last drop before 11 PM.
steps.time: Last run at the hub before 11 PM
steps.detail: Every run is its own case, its own manifest, and its own two signatures at each end. The first run leaves as soon as the Portfolio Manager's review is done, early enough for the last one to make it. A run that cannot reach the hub before 11 PM does not leave the site. On Thursday every factory phone goes, even from a site that keeps its phones on other nights.
steps.check: Every phone that recorded today is signed for at the hub, and the last drop is timed before 11 PM.

steps.do: In the morning, take back only the phones the hub has cleared, count them against the new manifest, and sign custody again.
steps.time: Early morning, early enough to be at the site before 7:00 AM
steps.detail: The attendant has confirmed on the dashboard that every phone's upload finished, charged them, and repacked them by site with a new manifest inside each case. Count against it before you sign. A phone the hub is holding stays at the hub, even if the site is short: a phone leaves the hub empty or it does not leave. The attendant reads you the ID of every held phone and why; write them down for the anchor. The third rule and the road rules hold on the way back.
steps.check: Every phone in the case is on the new manifest, both signatures are on the pickup line with the time out, and the held IDs are written down.

steps.do: Drive straight back to the site and hand the case to the anchor who opens the device room, custody signed, before 7:00 AM.
steps.detail: The anchor counts the phones against the manifest in the case and both of you sign. No signature, no handover. Tell them the held IDs, so a spare goes on that wearer's head today. The anchors clock in at 7:00 AM and recording starts at 8:00 AM; they never wait for the phones.
steps.check: The anchor's signature is on the drop line for every case, every cleared phone is at the site before 7:00 AM, and the anchor has the held IDs.

steps.do: Make sure every custody line from the night reaches the Portfolio Manager the same day, and keep nothing in the vehicle.
steps.detail: Every pickup and every drop is a custody event, and it goes into the registry the same day, never a verbal arrangement. The signed manifests are the proof of where each phone was at every hour of the night. Tell the anchor what was signed at the hub if the Portfolio Manager is not at the site. If you cannot run tomorrow night, call and message Moharam by 8 PM.
steps.check: The Portfolio Manager has every custody line from the night, and no phone, case, or paper is left in the vehicle.

done: Every phone that recorded today reached the hub in cases of a third or less, with two signatures on every custody line and the last drop before 11 PM, and every phone the hub cleared is back at the site with the anchor's signature before 7:00 AM.

fails.if: A run cannot reach the hub before 11 PM
fails.then: It does not leave. Call Moharam and the site's Portfolio Manager now. The phones that did not go stay locked in the device room on charge. The Portfolio Manager writes the backlog in device-days in the wrap report, and Moharam books the run that clears them. A site holding more than one device-day is an incident.

fails.if: The count in the case does not match the manifest
fails.then: Do not sign for the manifest's number. Count again by device number with the person across from you. At the site, the case does not move until the Portfolio Manager finds the phone or writes a new manifest; a phone missing goes to the Portfolio Manager now, and lost mode starts within the hour. At the hub, write the number you counted and the missing IDs, both of you sign that, and call Moharam from the hub now, before you leave. A phone missing between the site and the hub has today's footage on it, so the clock is the hour, not the morning. Nobody wipes it first.

fails.if: Police stop you at a checkpoint
fails.then: Pull over and stay calm. Hand over the letter, the commercial register copy, and the manifest. Give the exact count. Call Moharam from the checkpoint: where you are, who is asking, what they want. Never argue, never hide the count, never name the client. If the phones or the papers are held, get a written receipt and tell Moharam. Mano brings counsel and documents the visit the same day, and the site's Portfolio Manager hears the same hour if the phones will be late.

fails.if: The vehicle is stolen or crashed
fails.then: Get yourself safe. If anyone is hurt, the injury comes first. Then call Moharam now: where you are, what happened, the count on the manifest. The quartermaster locates every phone on the MDM and puts them in lost mode within the hour. Nobody wipes first. You go with Moharam for the police report the same day, with the manifest and the commercial register copy. Replacements come from the spare pool before the next shift, and Moharam reviews the run within 24 hours: a third or less, the case locked and unmarked, custody signed, before 11 PM.

fails.if: The hub's line is down, or Moharam sends you to the second hub
fails.then: Drive to the hub Moharam names, and nowhere else. Same case, same manifest, custody signed at the second hub's drop. You hear it before you leave the site, and runs still end at 11 PM. Never upload through someone's home to get around it; a tested hub or a day-pass location, nothing else.

fails.if: The hub has not cleared a phone by morning
fails.then: It stays at the hub. Take only the cleared phones on the new manifest. The attendant tells the site's Portfolio Manager the held IDs before 7:00 AM, and you tell the anchor at the drop, so the site starts those wearers on spares. A phone leaves the hub empty or it does not leave.

escalate: Moharam, now, from the road or the site, at any hour; if a phone or a paper is held, Mano brings counsel the same day
